title: Food Service Technician
raw_text:
8-922. MOS 922A--Food Service Technician
   a. Licensing/certification requirement. None.
   b. Prerequisites. DA Cir 601 series.
   c. MOS 922A. MOS 922A is an accession MOS. The enlisted feeder MOS is 92G.
   d. Associated SQI.
        (1) 0--No special qualifications.
        (2) 8--Instructor.
        (3) P--Parachutist.
        (4) T--Transition (personnel only).
        (5) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
   e. Associated ASI. (Note: Refer to table 6-6 for (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all
warrant officer MOS)).
   f. Qualifications.
        (1) WO1/CW2 must--
              (a) Successfully complete the Food Service Technician Warrant Officer Basic Course
(WOBC).
              (b) Have 20/20 correctable vision and normal color discrimination per AR 40-501.
              (c) Have normal hearing.
              (d) Be a U.S. citizen. Qualify for a security clearance of SECRET.
              (e) A physical demands rating of Moderate (Gold).
              (f) A minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) – 0120 cm, Seated Power
Throw (PT) – 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) – 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) – 0036
shuttles in Physical Demand Category in “Moderate” (Gold).
        (2) CW3 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(1).
              (b) Successfully complete the Food Service Technician Warrant Officer Advanced
Course (WOAC).
        (3) CW4 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(2).
              (b) Successfully complete the Warrant Officer Staff Course (WOSC).
        (4) CW5 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(3).
              (b) Successfully complete the Warrant Officer Senior Staff Course (WOSSC).
   g. Duties.
        (1) WO1/CW2--
              (a) Serves as a technician or technical manager in a narrow technical functional area,
generally as the Brigade/Group Food Service Technician or as the Assistant Division Food
Service Advisor. Additionally, can serve as an Installation Food Program Manager.
              (b) Manages personnel, equipment and facilities to implement the Army Field
Feeding System, in training and mobilization during peace and wartime.
              (c) Advises commanders on matters pertaining to the Army Field Feeding System
and Theater of Operations.
              (d) Supervises to subordinate unit dining facilities and field kitchens.
              (e) Trains military and civilian personnel in procurement, storage, preparation and
serving of food.
              (f) Coordinates with Troop Issue Subsistence Activity (TISA) and Field Ration Break
Point to ensure smooth and efficient flow of rations to dining facilities and field kitchens.
              (g) Plan, train, oversees and evaluates ration break operations at all levels in the
acquisition, receipt, storage, ration configuration, shipments, accountability for subsistence,
water, ice religious operational rations, health and comfort packs in garrison, field training and
theater of operations.
              (h) Conducts surveys of food, equipment, personnel and facilities.
              (i) Budgets for and requisitions supplies and equipment to include replacing
equipment through life-cycle management. Prepares reports on design deficiencies in equipment
and facilities.
               (j) Coordinates with preventive medicine, veterinary and nutritional personnel on
sanitation, nutritional surveys and in menu testing.
              (k) Interprets and disseminates food service information, inspects field and
installation food service operations and provides technical assistance to non-appropriated fund
food service activities.
              (l) Provides technical advice to the commander and staff during preparation of
operational plans.
        (2) CW3--
              (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(1).
              (b) Serves in positions requiring a level of independence from supervision; such as
the Division Food Service Advisor or as Command Food Service Technician for an Area Support
Group or Corp Support Group.
              (c) Advises on matters pertaining to the establishment of programs in the culinary
arts for Army food service personnel.
        (3) CW4--
              (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(2).
              (b) Serves as the senior Food Service Technician in positions requiring advanced
level staff and technical skills; generally at the Corps or MACOM level, positions requiring
independence from supervision.
              (c) Instructs and provides technical advice to other countries in the development and
management of their food service program.
        (4) CW5--
              (a) Perform duties described in paragraph g(3).
              (b) Serves as the most senior Food Service Technician in positions which require an
unusual depth and breadth of technical knowledge for functional training and curriculum
development or major systems integration skills.
              (c) Develops reviews and updates the life-cycle management for all Food Service
warrant officers.
              (d) Advises MACOM commanders dealing in force modernization, personnel
management, logistic support analysis, integrated logistics support and integrated food service
support.
              (e) Serves in positions such as the Army's Food Advisor, MACOM Food Service
Technician or may be selected to serve in QM branch MOS immaterial positions such as the
career manager at AHRC or as Chief Warrant Officer of the Quartermaster Corps. Additionally,
may be selected to serve in Army Warrant Officer immaterial positions at the DA level.
   h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
        (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate.
        (2) Table 8-922A-1. Physical requirements.
        (3) Authorized position titles are provided in appendixes B and C. The following grades are
used to code positions into one of four definable skill levels: W2 equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals
CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The grades are listed in the following standards of
grade tables:
              (a) Table 8-922A-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
              (b) Table 8-922A-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
